summary: Tests-writing run for issue #39 (adopt generated OpenAPI client + enforce solver parity with the parity corpus). Committed: (1) vendored byte-identical copy of the upstream parity corpus (viamin/color_matching priv/parity/v1/corpus.json, algorithm_version 1) as a test fixture; (2) SolverParityCorpusTests — permanent unit test suite replaying all 12 corpus scenarios through WeightedSquaredErrorScorer and the CompositionSolver fast path with exact (==) score/selection/tie assertions; (3) PaletteAPIClientMigrationContractTests — characterization tests pinning the /api/v1 wire contract (paths, auth, error mapping, envelope decode) that the swift-openapi-generator migration must preserve; (4) docs/solver-parity-corpus.md — corpus provenance, refresh command, parity findings, and /api/v1 shape findings vs the published OpenAPI spec. Caveat: no Swift toolchain exists in this container (no swift/swiftc/docker), so swift test could not be executed here; parity logic was instead cross-verified by a Python reference implementation of the scorer semantics over the corpus (12/12 scenarios agree exactly, including ties, exclusions, zero-weight and unknown-weight handling), and the Swift suite was desk-checked against the current public ColorComposerCore API. The generated-client migration itself (Package.swift + Sources changes) is intentionally deferred to the implementation run per the tests-only phase rules.

The migration guard is in place: 8 new characterization tests pin exact request paths (/api/v1/printer_profiles, /api/v1/colors?printer_profile_id=N), Accept/bearer headers, 401->unauthorized, non-2xx->badStatus, malformed->malformedResponse, and envelope decoding incl. the embedded printer_profile that feeds the cached-profile fallback; the pre-existing 40+-case ProfileColorCacheTests pins per-server/profile disk-cache keying and offline fallback semantics. Swift toolchain unavailable in container, so the new suite was not executed locally.
